purpose: Define the minimum machine-verifiable evidence envelope required before any WS-BOEING-01 external gate may transition from missing/partial to complete/verified.
global_transition_rules: Only complete or verified are closed states.
A closed-state transition requires an external evidence envelope; internal CI success alone is insufficient.
The evidence source must be externally authorized or independently produced as required by the specific gate.
Every retained source artifact must have an immutable identifier and SHA-256 digest or equivalent cryptographic content digest.
The external authority and its role must be recorded; Worldshepherd author/operator cannot act as the independent reviewer.
Claims allowed by the evidence must be explicitly bounded and claims not allowed must remain explicit.
A single evidence envelope cannot close a broader gate than its documented scope.
If provenance, authority, scope, or digest cannot be verified, the transition is denied.
Preparation artifacts have contact_gate_effect=NONE and cannot be promoted into external evidence by relabeling.

forbidden_substitutes: review of protocol without relevant evidence

contact_gate_effect: NONE. Defining a transition contract closes no external gate; it only prevents unsupported future gate promotion.
claims_boundary: This contract is governance logic, not Boeing/Spirit engagement, authorization, data access, partner pilot evidence, measured effect, security/compliance validation, independent review, certification, adoption, savings, defect reduction, or remediation probability.
